q: Do renewable energy loans to MSMEs count as priority sector lending in India?
title: Are MSME solar loans priority sector?
short: Usually yes. A bank loan to a Udyam-registered micro, small or medium enterprise counts under the MSME category of priority sector lending whatever it funds, including solar or other renewable energy. A separate renewable energy category covers loans to borrowers for solar, biomass, wind and micro-hydel generation up to a per-borrower ceiling set in RBI's Master Directions.
audience: MSME owners, bank and NBFC credit teams

ul: MSME category: loans to enterprises classified as micro, small or medium under the MSMED Act, as evidenced by Udyam registration. The purpose of the loan does not need to be green; a rooftop solar plant, a new boiler or working capital all qualify.

Renewable energy category: loans to borrowers for solar power generators, biomass power generators, windmills, micro-hydel plants and non-conventional energy based public utilities such as street lighting and remote village electrification, up to a per-borrower limit. A separate, lower limit applies to individual households.
Ask your bank which of the two categories it reports your loan under.

sections.h: Which route applies to your loan
p: If you hold a Udyam certificate, the bank will normally classify your solar or efficiency loan under MSME, where there is no renewable energy ceiling. The renewable energy category matters mainly for borrowers that are not MSMEs, such as a project company or a larger firm setting up captive generation, and for households.

The per-borrower renewable energy ceiling, and the lower limit for individual households, are set in RBI's Master Directions on Priority Sector Lending and have been revised over time. Check the current Master Direction on rbi.org.in for both limits before you rely on them.

sections.h: How this differs from green deposits and green loans
ul: Priority sector status is a bank's regulatory classification. It can make a lender keener to lend, but it does not by itself lower your interest rate.
Green deposits (RBI framework, 2023) are money banks raise from depositors and must allocate to listed green activities, including renewable energy. That is separate from PSL.
A green loan in the market sense follows the Green Loan Principles: use of proceeds, project selection, management of proceeds and reporting. A loan can be PSL, green, both or neither.

senseible: Senseible does not decide priority sector classification; that is the bank's call under RBI rules. Its green loan readiness check and document-backed emissions record help you show a lender what the loan will change.
